thread:
Alex: Quick thought — can we try alternating the weekly triage so odd weeks are 'bug deep-dive' and even weeks are 'RFC/design micro-review'? My reasoning: reduces context-switch and gives space for owner follow-ups. :spiral_calendar:

Maya: +1 from me. Can we keep it to 30m? folks tend to drop off after 45.

Sam: agree on 30m. Suggest agenda: 5m quick wins, 15m triage, 5m rollouts/blocks, 5m RFC quick checks. If an RFC needs more time, spin out a follow-up meeting.

Kevin: question — how do we handle bug queue prioritization? current triage is messy. propose a tiny script to snapshot top 20 by severity and age and attach to the agenda.

Alex: good call. pasted a small agenda + snapshot command below — we can wire it into the calendar invite or a bot.

```
# Agenda (30m)
- 0-5m  Quick wins / blockers (anyone)
- 5-20m Bug triage (top 12 by severity/age) — assign owners inline
- 20-25m Rollouts / oncall handoffs / hotfixes
- 25-30m RFC quick checks + follow-ups (decide who needs a deep-dive)

# Quick snapshot (example)
python tools/bug_snapshot.py --limit 20 --sort severity,age --out /tmp/triage_snapshot.json
```

Priya: I like the rotation idea. Also suggest rotating the meeting lead each week so different squads bring issues. 2-week rotation seems reasonable.

Sam: can we add a one-line "pre-read" checklist for RFC weeks: link to RFC, key decisions needed, and a short context paragraph. That will keep RFC weeks efficient.

triage-bot: Daily backlog count: 42 open bugs. No P0 incidents. :robot_face:

Maya: I'll update the calendar invite (title + description) and add the agenda template. Will ping potential leads to confirm rotation schedule. Change goes live next Monday unless objections.

Kevin: :thumbsup:

Alex: vote — react with :white_check_mark: if you support, :x: if not.

Sam: :white_check_mark:

Priya: :white_check_mark:

Maya: :white_check_mark:

Kevin: :white_check_mark:

Alex: Sweet. I'll post a follow-up thread with the rotation roster and the automation link. Thanks all. :tada:
